release.body:
Checkwash v0.12.0 refuses repair evidence to weakened tests, reads `mock.ANY` as a tautology, and tags the release at its Action commit. The findings envelope stays at version 2 and the IR at version 3. Details are in the [release guide](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/v0.12.0/docs/releases/v0.12.0-public-launch.md), and the [versioned known issues](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/v0.12.0/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES-v0.12.0.md) disclose the remaining limits. A pass is not a correctness guarantee.

**Repair evidence refused (D-199).** Up to 0.11.0, an edit that changes nothing, such as `+ 0` in a function a test calls, could hold a weakened test at warn, which passes at the default threshold (#419). In a Python test or conftest, a weakened, removed, skipped or loosened assertion, a deleted test, a stand-in for the code under test, a normalized subject, a changed subject input and an expectation derived from the input now take no repair evidence, as a broad `except` already did (D-176); in a JS/TS test, a weakened or loosened assertion, a broad catch, a skip added to a live test and a table left with no row to run take none. Each such finding blocks beside any production change, a no-op one included, unless another compensation holds it, such as a compatibility `skipif`, a mild weakening inside the exact family or a deletion beside a removed symbol; a finding that a production change reached is labelled `REPAIR_EVIDENCE_REFUSED`. This blocks honest changes too: a feature or deprecated API removed together with an assertion or a test on it, a test rewritten beside a behaviour change where checkwash reads the rewrite as a weakened or removed assertion, an optional-dependency skip (`pytest.importorskip`, a `find_spec` `skipif`) added beside the change that needs it, and a test moved unchanged to another file but now importing its subject from the module that defines it, beside a fix to the code it tests, a move checkwash does not credit. Each needs a reviewed exemption (`checkwash allow`, merged to the base first). Some weakenings still pass by default, among them a rewritten expected value or a substituted assertion beside a no-op edit, and in JS/TS a removed assertion or test; the known issues list them.

**Three more holes, closed in part (D-201).** An equality with `unittest.mock.ANY` as a whole operand is read as a tautology, so rewriting an expected value into `ANY` is `ASSERT_WEAKENED`, with or without a dependency bump. A single test's skip earns the compatibility credit only when its condition is provably false in some environment of the matrix (CPython 3.11 to 3.14 and PyPy 3.11, each platform's two machines) and the gates a change adds, with the gates the test had, still leave such an environment; checkwash now assumes that a part of the condition it cannot read may be true, where 0.11.0 let it stand in for false. `assertEqual`, or a bare `assert ==`, rewritten as `assertCountEqual` on the same subject is `SUBJECT_NORMALIZED`. This blocks honest changes too: a skip that joins a platform or version check by `or` to a dependency's version, an environment variable or another condition checkwash cannot read, a gate spelled in a way checkwash does not read, a gate that leaves a test running only on Pythons older than 3.11 or only on a machine or interpreter outside the matrix, an expected value made `ANY` because it became generated, and a test made order-blind on purpose with `assertCountEqual`. `ANY` reached through a parametrize column, a fixture, another module's constant or a call, or wrapped in another comparison, still passes beside a version bump or a production change; the known issues list these.

**Exemptions across the upgrade.** An expected value rewritten into `ANY`, which 0.11.0 reported as `EXPECTATION_DEFINITION_CHANGED` or not at all, is now `ASSERT_WEAKENED`, and an ordered equality rewritten as `assertCountEqual` is a new `SUBJECT_NORMALIZED` finding. These carry new fingerprints, so an exemption recorded for an old finding does not cover them ([upgrade notes](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/v0.12.0/docs/embedding.md#v0110-to-v0120)). Neither D-199 nor D-201's skip rule moves fingerprints, so an existing exemption still applies to the findings they now block. Values inside an IR can differ for the same input; the IR version stays 3.

**The tag at the Action commit (D-200).** From this release the tag points at the release's Action commit A (`532f74ab070a924b23e2cc70e5d0091a05d8401d`), the commit the README on `main` recommends as the Action pin once this release is publicly verified, instead of at the release merge M (`ffaf4ed86ecc2baeb8cc008487a44d8495da9177`); the tag message names M on one line, `Release-Merge: <M>`. The PyPI package and the pyz are built from M, whose `doctor` differs from A's only in its own Action pin line, set to A. Install the CLI from PyPI or the pyz: a CLI installed through Git from the tag is A's; it reports the same version, and its `doctor` rejects the release's own Action pin. `check`, the Action, pre-commit and the Claude Code hooks never import `doctor`, so they run the same at A and at M. The source archives on this page are A's tree. Pin updaters such as Dependabot and Renovate, zizmor and `git ls-remote` now see the recommended pin as the tag's commit (inferred from those tools' documentation, not run). v0.11.0 stays as published. `doctor` 0.11.0 accepts only v0.10.0's and v0.11.0's Action pins and rejects the 0.12.0 pin (exit 1), and `doctor` 0.12.0 accepts v0.11.0's pin and its own, so upgrade the CLI and its local hooks before the Action pin, as before. The release-event and public-visitor stages, which run after this Release is published, run under the new tag rule for the first time; a tag cannot be moved, so a failure there may cost a v0.12.1.

**What was measured.** The fixed-corpus comparison checked 3,600 in-sample commits on LAPTOP-01AGNPJU (Windows, CPython 3.11.9, `HUMAN_AUTHORIZED_LOCAL_PJU_NOT_EC_POOL`), with the published v0.11.0 zipapp and with the candidate engine. No commit moved from block to pass, or to or from an error; 19 moved from pass to block (8 Python, 11 JS/TS). Eighteen are the commits D-199 listed when it measured its cost, among them deprecated APIs or a dependency removed with assertions on them, tests rewritten or skipped beside a behaviour change or a new default, and three security-advisory fixes whose tests now assert the corrected, opposite behaviour; the nineteenth adds a Python 3.14 skip to four tests already skipped on 3.11 to 3.13, which then run only on Pythons older than the matrix (D-201). Twelve more commits kept their verdict with different reports. On D-088's 1,263 skip, xfail and conftest commits, measured on earlier main commits, D-199 moved 53 from pass to block and D-201 2 more, none adjudicated. Neither set holds an `== ANY` or an `assertCountEqual` rewrite, so those rules' cost is unmeasured. An honest broad `except` around an assertion in a Python test or conftest, beside an opaque production change, still blocks unless checkwash proves it a failure relay, as in 0.11.0; how often history holds one is not measured, and Claude accepts that risk for 0.12.0 only, as a delegated decision. The verdict gate reports one case labelled pass that now blocks: a JS/TS `expect(value).toBeNull()` rewritten as `expect(value).to.exist` beside a production change, which v0.11.0 held at warn by repair evidence and D-199 now refuses. The gate reports such a move without failing; the label, written before D-199, has not been revisited. The three uvloop inputs that v0.10.0 blocked still pass with no finding. These are in-sample outcome counts, not a held-out or adjudicated false-positive rate.

**How it was released.** Release evidence for every stage is collected on LAPTOP-01AGNPJU (Windows, Python 3.11.9) and recorded as `HUMAN_AUTHORIZED_LOCAL_PJU_NOT_EC_POOL`: the pull request, main and tag stages before this Release, and the release-event and public-visitor stages after it. Native Linux, macOS and other Python versions are NOT_RUN for the release receipts; that gap is accepted for v0.12.0 only under the maintainer's pre-1.0 delegation and does not change the standing release contract. Separately, on the same machine, the full test suite passed on the release merge M's tree in six local legs (Windows CPython 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, and Linux CPython 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 in Docker), and the six corpus outputs were byte-equal; that run is supplementary evidence, not a release receipt, and macOS was not run. Claude (Claude Code) carried out this release under that delegation. The maintainer approved the release merge and reviewed the comparison's 19 moved commits and the gate's reported case before the tag, and the PyPI deployment waits for the maintainer's own approval.

GitHub assets, PyPI publication and verification of the actual public bytes are separate steps. The PyPI description, built from M, shows the install commands and Action pin of v0.11.0, the release verified before this one; the README on GitHub moves them to 0.12.0 once the public files are verified. The advertised CLI and Action pins advance from v0.11.0 only after public artifact and visitor verification, as the [release procedure](https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/blob/v0.12.0/docs/RELEASING.md) requires.
